name: Saba
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record for Saba (saba1276) and its reference links (Lovestrand 2012; Jungraithmayr & Peust 2019 on Gàlì/Miltu, not Saba; ElCat 2022)
sources.note: Bibliographic only; confirms Jungraithmayr 2020 is the sole descriptive (phonology-typed) reference.

sources.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann. 2020. Préliminaires à une étude du saba, langue tchadique orientale du Tchad (région de Melfi). Afrika und Übersee 93: 281-298. DOI 10.15460/auue.2020.93.1.221
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2 'Notes phonologiques' (pp. 283-284) covers vowels (2.1), consonants (2.2) and tones (2.3: two level tones L/H plus a falling HL contour, with minimal pairs); no mention of stress/accent anywhere in the article (the only 'accent' token is 'L'accent principal est mis sur...' in the résumé, i.e. the article's focus). Author states (p. 282) that no prior linguistic study of Saba exists.

sources.note: Closest-relative description (Sokoro, same subgroup, ~50% intercomprehension per Jungraithmayr 2020 fn. 2); not Saba itself, but the only other primary East Chadic B.3 source by the same author and may carry a prosody remark transferable as a family-level expectation only.
